internal_claims.claim: Northbridge has historically treated molten salt reactor (MSR) developers as a distinct sub-thesis from light-water SMR designs, due to a different regulatory pathway and added fuel-cycle and materials-corrosion technical risk that MSR designs carry.

Northbridge's technical advisor (informal call notes, not a formal diligence report) assessed MSR designs as technically compelling on paper — citing better passive safety characteristics and higher thermal efficiency than single-loop SMR designs.
The same technical advisor view held that MSR designs carry meaningfully longer time-to-commercial-demonstration than single-loop SMR designs, estimated at 5+ years further out.

This MSR assessment is explicitly noted as informal (advisor call notes) rather than a formal diligence report, meaning Northbridge has not run a full diligence process specifically on an MSR developer.

Separately from the MSR-specific view, Northbridge took a first pass at advanced nuclear roughly eighteen months ago and passed on two SMR (light-water, not MSR) developers, primarily due to regulatory-timeline risk — both companies assumed a faster NRC licensing path than the firm believed realistic given the design certification backlog at the time.

Two of Northbridge's largest LPs have asked about the firm's advanced nuclear exposure in recent quarterly update calls, citing rising corporate interest in nuclear-powered data center offtake agreements; this demand-side signal postdates and did not factor into the original SMR pass decision.

In the firm's quarterly cross-sector scan, inbound deal flow tagged 'advanced nuclear' (SMR and MSR combined) was up noticeably quarter-over-quarter, attributed by the sourcing team largely to the corporate data-center offtake narrative rather than to underlying technology changes — this is directional/informal market chatter, not a verified finding.

external_claims.claim: Molten salt reactor companies raised $353M in equity funding across 3 rounds in 2026 through April 2026
Global nuclear energy startup venture investment totaled over $4.5 billion across 81 companies so far in 2026, putting the year on pace to exceed 2025's record of $6.2 billion
Dutch molten salt reactor startup Thorizon raised €20 million ($21.7 million) in March 2025, led by Invest-NL, to advance its Thorizon One pilot reactor
A US government safety design approval for a molten salt reactor was granted, reported by World Nuclear News on July 22, 2026, tied to an executive order signed by President Trump in May 2025

The NRC issued a Safety Evaluation Report approving Terrestrial Energy's IMSR Principal Design Criteria, announced around May 12, 2026, following an earlier September 2025 approval of the Principal Design Criteria Topical Report
Executive Order 14300 directs the NRC to reach a final decision on an application to construct and operate a new reactor of any type within 18 months
Terrestrial Energy reported $289.9 million in cash and investments as of March 31, 2026, in its Q1 2026 results
The State of Texas allocated $120 million to support Natura Resources' MSR-1 project, and Natura Resources had secured $120 million in equity capital as of October 2025
The Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) agreed to buy up to 50 megawatts of electricity from Kairos Power's advanced molten-salt-cooled reactor, Hermes-2

Copenhagen Atomics received €2.5 million ($2.9 million) in EU grant funding, reported July 4, 2025, to support continued technological development and prototype validation of its thorium molten salt reactor
Seaborg's 250 MW-thermal (100 MWe) Compact Molten Salt Reactor (CMSR) is projected to have a US$70 million delivered cost as of 2025

Idaho National Laboratory (INL) projects future advanced reactor costs, including designs tested there, could decrease to between $0.09/kWh and $0.33/kWh after demonstration, licensing and deployment experience
A techno-economic analysis estimated the overnight capital cost of a 291 MWe Integral Molten Salt Reactor plant at $3,792/kW

Terrestrial Energy's own risk disclosures explicitly flag potential delays, cost overruns and contractor performance issues as risks to IMSR plant development, manufacturing and construction, as stated in its Q4 2025 (4Q25) earnings presentation dated March 30, 2026

A 2022 Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists analysis argues molten salt reactors, based on a 1960s Oak Ridge National Lab experiment, faced significant technical trouble then and the article contends similar issues remain unresolved today
